text:
Maya: Customer (acme) reporting intermittent 500/504 and large tail latency spikes (~5–30s) on dedicated inference pool ded-gpu-eu-1. They provided a few request ids: req_63a8f2b4, req_63a8f2f0, req_63a90012. Can someone help with repro steps and which logs to pull?

Ethan: Oncall here — thanks. Can you paste one full request-id and approximate UTC time? Also which pod/node name if available?

Maya: Timestamp around 2026-03-16T14:02:18Z. Pod prefix inference-svc-acme-xyz (full pod: inference-svc-acme-xyz-7f6d9). Example request id: req_63a8f2b4. Customer ran this curl locally (redacted key):

```bash
curl -v 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" 
  -H "x-request-id: req_63a8f2b4" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"gpt-xyz","input":"short prompt","max_tokens":128}' 
  https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate
```

They said the connection hangs ~15–20s then returns a 504.

Priya: For dedicated repro we need both pod and node data. Please collect (from support run or ask customer to run):
- `kubectl -n acme logs inference-svc-acme-xyz-7f6d9 -c runtime --since=30m > pod.runtime.log`
- `kubectl -n acme describe pod inference-svc-acme-xyz-7f6d9 > pod.describe.txt`
- `kubectl -n acme get events --sort-by='.metadata.creationTimestamp' > events.txt`
- `journalctl -u kubelet -n 1000 > kubelet.log`
- `sudo dmesg | tail -n 400 > dmesg.tail`
- `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,temperature.gpu,memory.used --format=csv -l 1 -f 10 > gpu-sample.csv` (run for ~30–60s around a repro)

Also capture prometheus scrape for GPU/node metrics if available: `curl http://localhost:9100/metrics | egrep 'nvidia|gpu|nvml' > node.metrics`

Ethan: From inside the cluster is helpful to rule out networking (LB) vs runtime. Try: 

```bash
kubectl exec -n acme -it inference-svc-acme-xyz-7f6d9 -- 
  curl -vv -H 'x-request-id: req_63a8f2b4' \'http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/generate\' -d @payload.json --max-time 60
```

That shows internal path latency. Also: `kubectl get pod inference-svc-acme-xyz-7f6d9 -o yaml | grep restartCount`

Maya: Customer uploaded partial logs: https://acme.s3.amazonaws.com/partial-logs/req_63a8f2b4-partial.tar.gz — grep shows an entry `worker loop waiting 19.8s` then `timeout`. GPU util in that window was ~5%.

rdr-bot: Support bundle created: bundle-98765. You can collect/upload with: `rdr-support collect --tenant acme --since 2026-03-16T13:50Z -o /tmp/acme-bundle-98765.tar.gz` then `rdr-support upload /tmp/acme-bundle-98765.tar.gz`.

Priya: Additional low-level captures that are very helpful if you can get them from the node: `top -b -n1 > top.out`, `iostat -x 1 5 > iostat.out`, `sar -n DEV 1 5 > net.sar`. Check `dmesg | grep -i Xid` and `grep -i oom /var/log/kern.log`. If you see Xid errors (GPU Xid), capture full kernel log around that timestamp.

Ethan: Also try `strace` on the worker process during a repro to catch syscalls blocked on io: `kubectl exec -n acme -it inference-svc-acme-xyz-7f6d9 -- apt-get update && apt-get install -y strace procps` then `kubectl exec -n acme -it inference-svc-acme-xyz-7f6d9 -- strace -f -p <pid> -o /tmp/strace.log` while firing the curl reproducer.

Maya: I'll ask Acme for permission to run those commands inside their pod (they said yes for support access). I'll coordinate a window and collect the bundle. I'll post the bundle link here when done.

Ethan: If this is impacting production, mark ticket P1 and I'll block time to look after you drop the bundle. When uploading, include the exact request ids (req_63a8f2b4, req_63a8f2f0, req_63a90012) and the UTC time range.

Maya: Uploaded bundle: https://support-uploads.redwood.internal/bundles/acme/98765.tar.gz and updated ticket TKT-4021. Quick grep for req_63a8f2b4 in pod.runtime.log shows: `2026-03-16T14:02:18Z worker loop waiting - queued tasks 0 - stall 19.812s` and `nvidia-smi snapshot during spike: utilization.gpu 4%`.

Priya: Low GPU utilization + worker stall points to CPU scheduling or blocking syscall (IO). Next set: collect `perf top` for 10s during repro and capture `strace` + `/proc/<pid>/stack` if possible. Also capture `cpuset`/cgroup cpu quota.

Ethan: Good. Keep this thread updated. I'll start a parallel debug on infra side to see if any node-level throttling events coincided with the UTC time range.

Maya: Will do, thanks — I’ll post the strace + perf output once we get the next spike. :thumbsup:
